by: Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only

question.population: Older adults with trouble sleeping (insomnia), or adults in general
question.outcome: Sleep (time to fall asleep, sleep time, sleep quality)

decisions.reason: RCTs of oral magnesium alone for sleep in adults match the question, but the results were synthesised narratively, not pooled.
Adults and magnesium vs placebo or low intake for sleep match, but observational studies are mixed with RCTs and nothing was pooled.
Pooled RCTs of oral magnesium vs placebo in older adults with insomnia, reporting time to fall asleep and total sleep time.
Meta-analysis of supplement RCTs on sleep quality, but magnesium trials were only discussed and not pooled because data were inadequate.
Title matches a meta-analysis of oral magnesium for insomnia in older adults, but this record is only a correction notice with no abstract; link it to the original review.
Covers magnesium and sleep quality, but it is a narrative review of mixed trials, some with extra ingredients and no stated placebo control, not a pooled analysis.

question.intervention: Oral magnesium taken every day to prevent attacks
question.outcome: How often migraine attacks happen and how bad they are

decisions.reason: Network meta-analysis of RCTs in adults with migraine includes a magnesium vs placebo comparison for prevention, reporting attack frequency and severity.
Pooled RCTs of supplements for migraine prevention, with a separate magnesium vs control analysis of attack frequency, severity and monthly migraine days.
Has a separate pooled analysis of 10 RCTs of oral magnesium vs control to prevent migraine, reporting attack frequency and intensity.

question.population: Adults with leg cramps that have no known cause, mostly older adults
question.outcome: How often cramps happen and how bad they are

decisions.reason: Pooled RCTs of oral magnesium versus control for cramp frequency, but only in pregnant women, not adults with idiopathic cramps.
Pooled RCTs of magnesium versus placebo or no treatment, including five trials in people with idiopathic cramps; cramp outcomes assessed.
Separate analysis of idiopathic cramps (mostly older adults) comparing magnesium with placebo on cramp frequency.

question.outcome: Pre-eclampsia, the baby's growth or birth weight, preterm birth or stillbirth

decisions.reason: Pooled RCTs of magnesium versus control in pregnancy, but in women with gestational diabetes as treatment, and the target outcomes are not clearly reported.
Women with gestational diabetes, and only glucose and lipid blood markers were pooled, with no pre-eclampsia, growth, preterm or stillbirth outcomes.
Oral magnesium versus control in pregnant women, but the outcome is leg cramps, not pre-eclampsia, growth, preterm birth or stillbirth.
Pooled RCTs of oral magnesium versus control in pregnant women for preventing pre-eclampsia.
Pre-eclampsia outcome, but only high-risk women, and just one magnesium trial among several micronutrients.
Women with gestational diabetes, magnesium only combined with zinc and calcium, and outcomes are oxidative stress markers.
Cochrane review of RCTs of oral magnesium versus placebo or no treatment in pregnancy, covering pre-eclampsia, SGA and perinatal mortality.
Pooled RCTs of oral magnesium versus placebo or control in pregnancy, reporting preterm birth, low birth weight and SGA.
Pooled RCTs of oral magnesium versus placebo in pregnancy, reporting preterm birth, low birthweight and SGA.
Protocol with no pooled results yet; it mainly studies magnesium levels, though a separate stream of supplementation RCTs will cover birth outcomes.
RCTs of magnesium in women with gestational diabetes, but outcomes are glycaemic and metabolic blood markers, not pre-eclampsia, growth or preterm birth.

question.population: Adults with or without high blood pressure

decisions.reason: Pooled RCTs of magnesium supplements versus placebo on blood pressure in adults with and without hypertension.
Pooled RCTs of magnesium and blood pressure, but only in people with type 2 diabetes, which is a narrower group.
Pooled placebo-controlled RCTs of magnesium on systolic blood pressure in normotensive adults, analysed separately from potassium.
Pooled RCTs of magnesium and blood pressure, but only in people with type 2 diabetes, which is a narrower group.
Pooled placebo-controlled RCTs of magnesium and blood pressure, but only in people with type 2 diabetes.
Pooled RCTs of magnesium and blood pressure, but only in people with insulin resistance, prediabetes or chronic diseases.
Meta-analysis of trials of magnesium supplements, with systolic and diastolic blood pressure as the main outcomes.
Narrative review of many nutraceuticals for blood pressure, with no pooled analysis of magnesium trials.
Pooled double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs of oral magnesium on blood pressure in normotensive and hypertensive adults.
Pooled RCTs of oral magnesium versus placebo or no treatment on blood pressure in adults with high blood pressure.
Magnesium was only given together with potassium or calcium, never on its own, in adults with high blood pressure.
Pooled randomised trials of magnesium supplements on blood pressure in people with and without high blood pressure.
Separate pairwise meta-analysis of oral magnesium vs placebo on SBP and DBP in adults without high blood pressure, which the population covers.
Magnesium supplements and blood pressure match, but this umbrella review pools effect sizes from 10 meta-analyses rather than pooling the randomised trials directly.

question.population: People with type 2 diabetes or at high risk of it
question.outcome: Fasting blood sugar, HbA1c or insulin resistance

decisions.reason: Pooled RCTs of oral magnesium vs placebo in people with diabetes and prediabetes, reporting insulin resistance, HbA1c and fasting glucose.
Women with PCOS only, and magnesium is pooled with other minerals rather than analysed alone against placebo.
Pooled RCTs of magnesium supplements in type 2 diabetes, reporting fasting blood glucose and HbA1c.
Looks at micronutrient status and ulcer healing in diabetic foot, not magnesium's effect on blood sugar or insulin resistance.
Pooled 24 RCTs of magnesium supplements in type 2 diabetes, reporting fasting glucose and HbA1c.
Pooled double-blind RCTs of oral magnesium vs placebo in people with or at high risk of diabetes, reporting glucose and insulin sensitivity.
Pooled RCTs of oral magnesium in type 2 diabetes, reporting HbA1c and fasting blood sugar.
Includes a separate pooled analysis of RCTs of magnesium in type 2 diabetes or high-risk people, reporting fasting glucose and HOMA-IR.
Network meta-analysis of RCTs in type 2 diabetes with magnesium as its own arm, reporting HbA1c, fasting blood sugar and HOMA-IR.
Outcome is blood lipids only, not blood sugar, HbA1c or insulin resistance.
Outcomes are blood pressure and body weight measures, not blood sugar or insulin resistance.
Pools diabetic and non-diabetic people together, and no matching diabetes-only glucose analysis is clearly reported.
Oral magnesium RCTs with glucose, HbA1c and HOMA-IR outcomes, but diabetic and general non-diabetic people are pooled together.
Pooled double-blind RCTs of oral magnesium vs placebo in people with or at high risk of diabetes, reporting glucose and HOMA-IR.
Umbrella review that combines earlier meta-analyses in type 2 diabetes instead of pooling the trials directly.
Outcome is blood pressure, not blood sugar, HbA1c or insulin resistance.
Reviews magnesium trials on insulin resistance across mixed clinical conditions without pooling the results.
Pooled double-blind RCTs of oral magnesium vs placebo in type 2 diabetes, reporting HbA1c and fasting glucose.
Pooled RCTs of oral magnesium versus placebo in prediabetic (high-risk) adults, reporting fasting glucose, HbA1c and HOMA-IR.
Population is type 2 diabetes, but outcomes are serum magnesium and calcium, not fasting glucose, HbA1c or insulin resistance.
A correction notice for a review of magnesium intake and diabetes or stroke risk, not supplement trials on glycemic outcomes.
Title describes a meta-analysis of double-blind RCTs of magnesium supplements on glucose metabolism in people with or at risk of diabetes.
Pooled RCTs of magnesium versus placebo or other comparator in type 2 diabetes, measuring fasting blood sugar and HbA1c.
Looks at various supplements for diabetic foot ulcer healing, including animal and observational studies, not glycemic outcomes.
Looks at antioxidant supplements and diabetic retinopathy, without pooled magnesium trials on glycemic outcomes.
